name: Ötztaler Höhenstraße
kurzbeschreibung: The Ötztal Glacier Road above Sölden ascends into the high-alpine glaciated peaks of Rettenbach and Tiefenbach as one of Europe's highest panoramic alpine routes.
preis: Toll road for cars and motorcycles (free with Ötztal Inside Summer Card)
oeffnungszeiten: Open mid-May to late October/early November (weather permitting)
beschreibung:
Überblick

The Ötztal Glacier Road (Ötztaler Höhenstraße) is one of the highest and most awe-inspiring paved mountain passes in Europe, unlocking direct access to the monumental glacier world of the Ötztal Alps. Commencing from the famed alpine resort of Sölden, the winding route navigates dramatic switchbacks up to the Rettenbach Glacier at 2,675 metres and continues through the Rosi-Mittermaier Tunnel—the highest road tunnel in the Alps at 1.7 kilometres in length—to terminate at the Tiefenbach Glacier at 2,830 metres elevation. Across fifteen exhilarating kilometres, motorists, motorcyclists, and intrepid cyclists conquer over 1,400 vertical metres framed by hanging icefalls, granite walls, and rugged moraines. Famous for hosting the FIS Alpine Ski World Cup opening races every autumn, the route offers breathtaking close-up vistas of glaciated summits including the towering Wildspitze.

Route & Anforderungen

Ascending the glacier road requires attentive driving and vehicles in excellent mechanical order, featuring sustained gradients exceeding eleven percent and steep pitches touching thirteen percent. The well-engineered asphalt highway rises steadily from the toll station above Sölden, tracing soaring switchbacks protected by rockfall galleries. Drivers and motorcyclists should use low engine gears on the descent to prevent brake overheating. For road cyclists, this climb represents a legendary bucket-list challenge widely regarded as one of the hardest ascents in international road biking. At the extensive glacier parking terminals, marked hiking trails lead to breathtaking vantage points, including the Schwarze Schneid viewing platform at 3,250 metres, which demands sturdy footwear, surefootedness, and warm windproof layers.

Besuch & Anreise

Access is via the Inntal autobahn A12 (exit Ötztal) and federal highway B186 south through Umhausen and Längenfeld to Sölden. At the southern edge of town, clear signage directs traffic onto the glacier mountain toll road. The road operates from mid-May through late autumn depending on snowfall. Frequent regional glacier shuttle buses run from Sölden, providing environmentally sustainable transit with fare exemptions for local guest card holders. Extensive free parking lots are available at both glacier terminals.

Tipps

Do not miss the dramatic cantilevered footbridge on the Schwarze Schneid, which commands views stretching all the way to the Italian Dolomites. Always check the morning mountain webcams and local weather reports before departing, as high-altitude conditions can shift rapidly even during midsummer.
